summary: Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Semencov studied at Moscow State University (1963) and Banaras Hindu University (1967–1968). He served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1968–1984) and the Institute of Philosophy (1984).

Ivanov worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Moscow State University under Mikhail Peterson and Pyotr Kuznetsov. He held posts at Moscow State University, the Institute of Slavic Studies, Stanford, Yale, Russian State University for the Humanities, and UCLA.

Vydūnas was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Königsberg, Greifswald, Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, and Berlin. He taught Lithuanian at Humboldt University of Berlin (1917–1919) and held a post at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1912–1940).

Machek specialized in linguistics and Indology, earning a Ph.D. at Charles University under Josef Zubatý and studying under Antoine Meillet, Theodor Bloch, and Sylvain Lévi. He was a librarian in Paris and became Docent at Masaryk University in 1931.
Jayasuriya was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

Rouse worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, earning a Doctor in Letters from Christ's College, Cambridge, where he studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He was Headmaster of The Perse School and served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at Christ's College.

A history and archaeology scholar, Rivers studied medicine at St Bartholomew's Hospital and the University of London. He was a Lecturer in Psychology at Cambridge, Fellow of St John's College, and President of the Royal Anthropological Institute.

Haskell specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth College and Yale University, where he completed his doctoral studies under William Dwight Whitney and served as a librarian from 1875 to 1905.

Johnson, an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Sussex and the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He held a fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford, and became Lecturer in Religious Studies at Cardiff University in 1992.

Brown worked in Indology and history/archaeology, studying at Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield and Franklin Edgerton. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Government Sri Pratap Memorial Rajput College of Commerce, and the University of Pennsylvania (1926–1966).

Kloetzli specializes in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from the University of Chicago (1964) with mentors including J. A. B. van Buitenen and Alf Hiltebeitel. He lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

A scholar in linguistics and Indology, Karunatillake served as Professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.
Tarn was a historian and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who was educated at Eton College and Trinity College, Cambridge, where he later served as a Fellow.

Samitharathana specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned an MA from SOAS University of London and an MPhil from the University of Oxford, where he became Founding President/Managing Trustee of the Oxford Buddhist Society in 2023.

A scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, Tam earned a PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He held posts at Hong Kong Polytechnic University and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, serving as professor and department chairperson.
Majewski was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Collegium Nobilium until 1785 and later taught there. In 1808, he was placed in charge of the Central Archives of Historical Records.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Rahula studied at Ceylon, Calcutta, and the Sorbonne under Paul Demiéville. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura and Professor of History and Religions at Northwestern University.

Fairservis worked in archaeology and Indology, studying at Chicago, Columbia, and Harvard (Ph.D.). He served as Director of the Burke Museum, held curatorial positions at the American Museum of Natural History, and taught at the University of Washington and Vassar College.

Cook was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Woodstock College, De Nobili College, St. Mary's College, and Georgetown University. He served as Professor of Linguistics at Georgetown University from around 1966 to 1993.

Henning worked in Iranian studies and linguistics, earning his Ph.D. at Göttingen under Friedrich Carl Andreas. He held positions at the Prussian Academy of Sciences, SOAS University of London, and the University of California, Berkeley.
